stem: How does the distribution of sleep stages change between the first and second halves of a typical night's sleep?

options.text: The first half has more REM sleep, while the second half has more slow-wave sleep.
The distribution of REM and non-REM sleep is uniform throughout the night.
The first half has predominantly slow-wave sleep, while the second half has more REM sleep.
Stage 1 sleep is only present in the second half of the night.

explanation: According to the hypnogram description, slow-wave sleep is concentrated in the first half, and REM sleep increases toward the second half.
rationale: Deep, slow-wave sleep generally occurs earlier to prioritize physical restoration.

optionExplanations.A: This is the reverse of the actual architecture; deep restorative sleep typically occurs earlier.
optionExplanations.B: Sleep architecture is cyclical and structured, with different stages predominating at different times.
optionExplanations.C: According to the hypnogram description, slow-wave sleep is concentrated in the first half, and REM sleep increases toward the second half.
optionExplanations.D: Stage 1 occurs at the onset of sleep and during transitions between cycles throughout the night.

source.hint: Deep, slow-wave sleep generally occurs earlier to prioritize physical restoration.
